Every scrolling logo strip in the sample is a marketing page — Headspace, Givingli, Zipline, Voiceflow, PayPal, Current, Pitch, Vizcom, Linear, Fiasco, Framer — pre-login, aimed at someone deciding whether to sign up; none appears inside a product, and even there the pattern earns manual controls (Headspace’s carries prev/next, because auto-motion alone cannot be read). Twelve in-app dashboards in an empty state — Depop, Navan, Canny, PayPal, Etsy, Shopify, Square, Kajabi, Kit, Hotjar, Expensify, Cofounder — show the broker’s own zeros and a next action; not one turns the empty dashboard into a pitch about platform size, because that argument is won before login. And the nine that do name supply in-app — Databricks’ Featured providers (Epsilon, FactSet, Moody’s, S&P Global, with Show all providers as the door), Whop, Eventbrite, Braintrust, Wix, Kit, Discord, X, Ghost — are all static, and every row is a link. A marquee also reveals its own supply: Vizcom’s repeats three logos to fill the width, and a visible loop under 1,500+ advertises scarcity rather than scale. Three details are load-bearing. A fact per row, not just a name — Eventbrite’s move (114 upcoming events): a name proves registration, institution type and loan range prove the lender is usable, and the row becomes the start of work rather than decoration. The tile is the squared muted institution mark, never the person’s navy circle — these rows are accounts, and the two grains must never read alike. And it sits inside the Lender network card, under the three figures, so the names read as evidence for the numbers directly above them and Browse lenders is already the door — a second one would have been the same duplicate-launcher collision that took the button off the trial band. The first draft was wrong about where (Tanya, 14 Sep): it went under the first-session network band in the main column and retired with it, on the argument that this is proof for day zero. That band was replaced the same day by the evergreen card one entry up, and evergreen is the better home — advertising new joiners is an ongoing job, not a day-zero one. [~] Two questions go to Tony with this, not yet sent: whether the figures above may stand once checkable names sit beneath them (Q83 already asks half of it), and whether registered institutions may be named as an advert to every broker — names are ungated in search under the never-gate list, but a broadcast panel is a different act from a search result and nothing recorded says lenders consented to it. Rows, ranges and join ages are sample data, as everywhere else here; live they come off the registered side the Source filter already names.
  • The research request got its fourth state and its two dates, 16 Sep [T] [💡 rec · Mobbin 16 Sep] [~] — the task doc’s row 17 names four Prospector contact states — Not requested · Researching (requested date, ETA) · Found (contact shown) · Not found (request refunded) — and the file drew three. Measured before the change, setting a request to found printed ↺ Request returned · Nobody found on the deal row and dropped the profile back to a Request again button: a search that had succeeded rendered as the failure and then offered to be run a second time, because the not-found arm was an else rather than a case. The reason on record for leaving the arrival undrawn was that it needs a notification surface (row 25); the file already notified the failure of the same request in the activity feed and in Needs attention, so the surface was never the blocker — what genuinely does not exist is email (question 78), and nothing added here claims one. Found now reads ✓ Contact found, fills the three cells the row had been explaining as empty (“the criteria live on a banker and there is no banker” — an argument that expires the moment there is one), names the person under the institution, and swaps the kebab’s Request again for an email action. The banker joins NETWORK rather than a store of its own: a parallel store was tried first and the prototype refuted it inside the hour, since the profile’s own new line read matched like any registered lender while the Matches tab did not list her — matching reads NETWORK, and so do eighteen other readers. Wade Kimball at Ironwood had settled it already, carrying src:"prospector" inside NETWORK since 31 Aug; he is the aftermath of a find with no record of the request that produced him, and Marisol Reyes is the same row with the other half attached. That is the opposite of S.myb, where a typed-in name has no criteria and can never be scored — and the difference is the paid button’s own promise, a named banker with their criteria. The second half is the dates, and they were contradicting each other. Three surfaces printed one request: the deal row and the quick view counted down (7 days left) while the profile named a day (due 20 Sep) — left was the constant 7 and due was the literal string “20 Sep”, so on a request placed 16 Sep the two were four days apart on one record, one click apart. The record carries two real dates now, ask and on, and one function (reqDates) turns them into the line, which is the only arrangement under which three surfaces cannot drift again. The countdown went with the contradiction. Across twenty shipped request lists every one prints the date the request was made and not one counts down: Selfridges Date submitted, Remote Added on, Oyster Created on, Aboard Requested, 7shifts Date submitted. Where a delivery estimate exists it is a date — adidas Expected delivery TUE, 17 JUNE, Fiverr should deliver this order by Nov 17, Walmart Arrives by Sat, May 24 — or a ceiling stated once over the whole queue, as Netflix’s can take up to 30 days sits above a table whose rows carry only Created On and Status. Tony’s seven days [T] (page inventory row 16, 27 Aug) is that ceiling, so it is printed as the day it falls on: Requested 16 Sep · expected by 23 Sep. The row itself calls the turnaround TBD; it is not, and has not been since August. One stale word died with it — the activity feed still read “returned your credit”, the last live sentence in the file speaking the retired unit, which the 15 Sep migration recorded as finished. It was one function away from the rows it swept. Amplify Credit Union is a third saved prospect so all four states stand on one screen instead of one at a time, and it is also the first Prospector row that is a credit union, exercising the NCUA-charter half of a line the template has carried since 31 Aug with nothing to fill it. Marisol, her criteria and both dates are sample, like every banker here. Still open: the tab badge reads Saved lenders 3 over six rows — it counts bankers and the tab holds institutions too — which predates this change and is the same one-unit-two-meanings problem the match counts were fixed for on 31 Aug.
